entries.test: Public evaluations of the described systems available in July 2022 would show whether their language comprehension approached human competence across syntax, semantics, and contextual interpretation.
entries.note: “Current” refers to July 2022. The surrounding discussion gives understanding a practical reading in terms of relating sentences to meanings.

entries.test: Public developmental research on three-year-olds’ language competence and exposure, alongside contemporary estimates of future GPT training inputs, would test the asserted mastery and input disparity.
entries.note: The main assertion concerns children’s existing abilities, not a forecast about GPT releases. “Might imagine” qualifies the comparison rather than making children’s mastery probabilistic.
This is a counterfactual claim about what successful performance would fail to guarantee. It does not predict that successful systems will actually use mechanisms different from humans.
